record.paper_title: Some Properties of and Open Problems on Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials
record.context_brief: Vanishing Conjecture for degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials
record.original_question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 over C whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. Let Delta be the Laplace operator on C[z], Delta = sum from i = 1 to n of D_i squared. Must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P (z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := (d^2P/dz_i dz_j) are nilpotent.

Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P (z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), Delta^m P^{m+1} (z) = 0 when m >> 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $\mathbb{C}[z]=\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$. For $f\in\mathbb{C}[z]$, define the Laplace operator $\Delta := \sum_{i=1}^{n} \partial^2/\partial z_i^2$, and for a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{C}[z]$ define the Hessian matrix $\operatorname{Hes} P := \left(\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\,\partial z_jight)_{1\le i,j\le n}$. A polynomial $P$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\operatorname{Hes} P$ is a nilpotent matrix (equivalently, all its eigenvalues, viewed in the function field, are zero).

Prove or disprove: for every homogeneous polynomial $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ of degree $4$ which is Hessian nilpotent, there exists an integer $M\ge 0$ such that
$$\Delta^{m} igl(P(z)^{m+1} igr)\;=\;0\qquad	ext{for all }m\ge M.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Vanishing Conjecture for homogeneous degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials is known to be equivalent to the Jacobian Conjecture (after work of Bass–Connell–Wright, Meng, Zhao). The Jacobian Conjecture remains an outstanding open problem, so this special case of the Vanishing Conjecture is likewise open as of the latest literature, with only partial results in low dimension or under additional hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials and the Jacobian Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the Jacobian Conjecture to a vanishing conjecture on iterated Laplacians of powers of homogeneous degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The degree-4 vanishing conjecture is equivalent to the Jacobian Conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Jacobian conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Jacobian conjecture is a famous unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Jacobian Conjecture, equivalent to the stated conjecture, is open.

status_evidence.title: A few remarks on the Generalized Vanishing Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses partial progress on generalized vanishing conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results on the Vanishing Conjecture are known.
